[[File:Wes_Moore_Official_Governor_Portrait.jpg|thumb|[[Wes Moore]] has been governor since January 18, 2023]]
The [[governor of Maryland]] is the [[head of government]] of the U.S. state of [[Maryland]]. The current governor is Democrat [[Wes Moore]], who took office on January 18, 2023.

== Governors ==
{{For|the period before independence|List of colonial governors of Maryland}}
Maryland was one of the original [[Thirteen Colonies]] and was admitted as a state on April 28, 1788.<ref>{{Cite report |title=Admission of States to the Union: A Historical Reference Guide |url=https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R47747 |access-date=October 20, 2026 |id=CRS Report no. R47747 |publisher=[[Congressional Research Service]] |date=December 17, 2024}}</ref> Before it declared its independence, Maryland was a [[Province of Maryland|colony]] of the [[Kingdom of Great Britain]].

Under the [[Maryland Constitution of 1776|constitution of 1776]], governors were appointed by the [[Maryland General Assembly]] to one-year terms.{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=1695|loc=1776 art. XXV}} They could be reelected for two additional terms, though they must take four years off after leaving office.{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=1696|loc=1776 art. XXXI}} An 1837 constitutional amendment allowed for popular election of governors to three-year terms,{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=1710|loc=1837 amend., § 20}} though they could not succeed themselves.{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=1711|loc=1837 amend., § 23}} The [[Maryland Constitution of 1851|1851 constitution]] removed the term limit, and lengthened terms to four years, to commence on the second Wednesday of January following the election.{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=1718|loc=1851 art. II, § 1}} Governors were limited to two consecutive terms beginning in 1948.<ref name="amend1948">{{Cite web |title=Governor |url=http://guide.msa.maryland.gov/pages/history.aspx?ID=SH54 |access-date=October 28, 2026 |website=Guide to Government Records |publisher=[[Maryland State Archives]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251206173343/https://guide.msa.maryland.gov/pages/history.aspx?ID=SH54 |archive-date=December 6, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The office of [[Lieutenant Governor of Maryland|lieutenant governor]] was created in 1864,{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=1750|loc=1864 art. II, § 6}} abolished in 1867, and recreated in 1970. The lieutenant governor succeeds to the office of governor should it become vacant. In the original constitution, the first named of the Governor's Council would act as governor if it were vacant, until a new governor was selected; this was changed to the [[Secretary of State of Maryland|secretary of state]] in 1837.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maryland Lieutenant Governor |url=https://msa.maryland.gov/msa/mdmanual/08conoff/ltgov/html/02ltgovf.html |access-date=October 28, 2026 |website=Maryland Manual On-Line |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251230175428/https://msa.maryland.gov/msa/mdmanual/08conoff/ltgov/html/02ltgovf.html |archive-date=December 30, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> The 1867 constitution originally called for the General Assembly to immediately elect a new governor; if they were not in session, the president of the Senate would act as governor until one was elected.{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=1786|loc=1867 art. II, § 6–7}}

|style="background:#EEEEEE; color:inherit;"|{{small|Lieutenant<br>governor<br>acting}}{{efn|Mandel named Lieutenant Governor Lee acting governor on June 4, 1977, as he was dealing with charges of mail fraud and racketeering, and citing health reasons;<ref>{{Cite news |last=Luxenberg |first=Steven M. |date=June 5, 1977 |title=Mandel Yields Power of Office to Lee |page=A1 |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun|The Sun]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-baltimore-sun-lee-becomes-acting-gov/132244649/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201055541/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-baltimore-sun-lee-becomes-acting-gov/132244649/ |archive-date=December 1, 2023 |url-status=live |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> he would be found guilty in August, and sentenced to four years in prison in October. He rescinded the designation on January 15, 1979, two days before the end of the term; he then made Lee acting governor again for a time on January 16 so he could preside at the installation of a judge on the Court of Appeals.<ref name="md-lee-blair" />{{sfn|Sobel|1978|p=685}}|name=mandel-lee}}
|style="background:#EEEEEE; color:inherit;"|''Acting as governor''
